Synopsis:
    Brent crude has broken above $100/bbl for the first time in six weeks, driven by escalating U.S.-Iran military conflict and Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure. Roughly 10 million bpd — ~10% of global demand — remain offline. Emergency reserves (U.S. SPR at 1982 lows, IEA 75% drawn) are largely depleted, leaving markets highly vulnerable to further shocks. Analysts warn the supply deficit is structural, not transitory, with a growing geopolitical risk premium embedded in prices.

Relevance: IMPLICIT — Hormuz disruptions threaten Qatari LNG export routes; high oil prices incentivise fuel-switching to gas in some sectors while simultaneously signalling broader energy scarcity.
